PullRequest.Title: Model router skill: quote examples that contain a colon
PullRequest.Body:
The model router skill now says to quote any route example or `when` text that contains `: `, such as a pasted error message.

Pasted errors make natural examples (`- CUDA error: device-side assert triggered`), but YAML reads an unquoted `error: detail` as a key and a value, so the router fails its check and the agent needs another round trip to fix it.

Scenarios.Scenario: Agent-host load and non-virtual Copilot session setup
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The module constructs the fixed model-router skill string once when loaded. Session setup creates and passes a SkillProvider to the Copilot SDK, but does not call readSkill or materialize an additional boundary operation because of the new sentence.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Pass the existing SkillProvider callback object in the SDK session configuration.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One provider handoff per non-virtual session, unchanged by the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same provider was created and passed for every eligible session with a slightly shorter module-level template.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The handoff remains on session construction, but the added skill sentence is not read or separately transferred at this point.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Agent-host process count and concurrent non-virtual sessions; the added static text is retained once per process, while provider objects remain one per session as before.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Session launches can occur concurrently, but each still creates one provider and the diff adds no task, queue, Promise, or fan-out.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The template is a module-level constant and therefore warm after module load. There is no positive/negative cache change, cache-key change, or new miss path.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the changed hunk is inside a module-level template, and traced session setup only passes the unchanged provider interface.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact SDK internals after receiving the provider are external, but repository code proves the diff adds no provider invocation or launch-time I/O; only a small fixed literal is added.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: fixed, process-level string growth is negligible and does not add startup work, I/O, or concurrency.

Scenarios.Scenario: Loading the model-router skill for an enabled session
Scenarios.CriticalPath: When the SDK requests the model-router skill, readSkill performs the existing single string replacement and returns the content. The new sentence increases that fixed response by only a small bounded amount before the SDK can use it.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Return the model-router skill text through the SDK SkillProvider callback for eventual model context use.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One returned string per SDK read request, unchanged; the payload grows by one bounded sentence.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same callback returned the same fixed template minus the added quoting guidance.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The in-memory replacement must finish before the skill can be consumed, but the added fixed bytes do not create a meaningful latency or allocation mechanism.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of model-router skill reads. Each read processes the same bounded template; cost does not scale with router count, workspace size, chat history, or user input.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Independent sessions may request skills concurrently, but there is no shared mutable resource, added Promise, limiter change, or burst introduced by the diff.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Repository code does not cache readSkill results; each existing read performs one replacement. The diff changes neither caching nor coalescing behavior and introduces no negative-cache state.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the only changed behavior is bounded string length; call count and replacement logic are unchanged.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The SDK's skill-read caching policy and invocation prevalence are not visible in-repository, but even a cold read adds only fixed bytes and no new operation.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: there is no unbounded serialization, repeated collection work, or boundary fan-out.

Scenarios.Scenario: Authoring and validating a model-router YAML file containing colon-space text
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The skill guidance is consumed before the model writes YAML; the existing workflow then invokes check_model_router. The added sentence does not add a validation call and is intended to avoid an invalid-YAML correction cycle.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read the selected router file during check_model_router validation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One file read for a path-based check; without a path, one read per already-discovered router, unchanged by the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The workflow already required check_model_router after every edit and performed the same read cardinality.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Validation waits for the existing read, but the new guidance does not add a check or file read and may prevent a later corrective check.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Serialize validation diagnostics and available model descriptions into the existing tool result.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One serialization per tool invocation, unchanged; output size continues to scale with existing router/model data rather than the added skill sentence.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same tool invocation serialized the same validation data; malformed colon-space examples could require an additional correction cycle rather than fewer cycles.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The existing tool result must return before authoring continues, but no extra invocation or larger result is introduced.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One edited router path per normal validation, or the effective number of discovered router files when the tool is intentionally called without a path. Neither cardinality is increased by the diff.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: A single-path check performs one file read. The no-path tool already checks discovered routers with Promise.all; the diff neither widens that set nor changes its existing parallelism.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache behavior is changed. Model enumeration and router discovery remain owned by the existing host callbacks; the prompt sentence creates no key, retained entry, miss retry, or invalidation path.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the changed instruction does not alter tool implementation, filesystem cardinality, or Promise.all concurrency.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Whether the language model follows the new instruction and how often users paste colon-space text are uncertain, but that uncertainty affects potential savings, not a regression mechanism.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: all expensive boundaries are pre-existing and unchanged, while the guidance plausibly reduces repeated authoring work.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over the sole changed hunk and traced module load, session/provider setup, skill delivery, and model-router validation. The PR adds a small fixed prompt sentence without new I/O, fan-out, cache state, concurrency, or scaling allocation, so no findings were submitted.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
